{{Short description|Estonian mycologist (1928–2012)}}
[[File:Erast Parmasto (seenevana) oli eesti mükoloog, ajakirja Loodus (97-01) aastapäeval 01.jpg|thumb|Erast Parmasto, 2001]]

'''Erast Parmasto''' (28 October 1928 – 24 April 2012)<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ut.ee/ial5/fce/fce49pdf/fce49_bresinsky.pdf |title=Erast Parmasto 1928–2012 in memoriam |access-date=2014-06-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140606231820/http://www.ut.ee/ial5/fce/fce49pdf/fce49_bresinsky.pdf |archive-date=2014-06-06 |url-status=dead }}</ref> was a noted [[Estonia]]n [[mycologist]], bioscientist and [[botanist]] and onetime director of the [[Estonian Institute of Zoology and Botany]].

Parmasto was born in [[Nõmme]]. He became a member of the Estonian Institute of Zoology and Botany in 1950 and served as its director from 1985 to 1990. His establishment of a mushroom [[herbarium]] in 1950 has since seen recognition of 160,000 samples, 37,000 of which Parmasto himself collected.<ref name="MOE">{{cite web|url=http://www.envir.ee/1068364|title=Eerik Kumari award won by mycologist Erast Parmasto|date=May 13, 2008|publisher=Estonian Ministry of the Environment|access-date=November 30, 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615140102/http://www.envir.ee/1068364|archive-date=June 15, 2011}}</ref>

Parmasto published more than 150 papers and 200 articles during his academic career and his works are commonly used in popular scientific and academic journals in Estonia.<ref name="MOE"/> He issued two [[exsiccata|exsiccatae]], namely ''Eesti seente eksikaat. Mycotheca Estonica. Gerbarij gribov Estonii'' (1957 to 1961) and ''Corticiaceae URSS'' (1965 to 1969).<ref>{{cite web |title=Eesti seente eksikaat. Mycotheca Estonica. Gerbarij gribov Estonii: IndExs ExsiccataID=749817788 |website=IndExs – Index of Exsiccatae |publisher=Botanische Staatssammlung München |url=https://www.botanischestaatssammlung.de/DatabaseClients/IndExs/Exsiccatae_IndExs_Details.jsp?ExsiccataID=749817788 |access-date=30 August 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Corticiaceae URSS: IndExs ExsiccataID=1744154367 |website=IndExs – Index of Exsiccatae |publisher=Botanische Staatssammlung München |url=https://www.botanischestaatssammlung.de/DatabaseClients/IndExs/Exsiccatae_IndExs_Details.jsp?ExsiccataID=1744154367 |access-date=30 August 2024}}</ref> His expertise in the field of [[mycology]] has resulted in him being nicknamed "Seenevana", or the "grand old man of mushrooms".<ref name="MOE"/>  As a mycologist, the field with which Parmasto was most associated, he was best known for his establishment and enhancement of databases for species of mushrooms within Estonia.<ref name="MOE"/> He was also the author of the first Estonian-language textbook on biosystematics in history.<ref name="MOE"/> 

Parmesto was furthermore one of the driving forces behind the establishment of [[Liiva-Putla Nature Reserve]], one of only five areas created for the protection of mushrooms in Europe.<ref name=keskkonnaamet>{{cite book | title = Natural Values of Saare County | year = 2012 | page = 12 | publisher = Estonian Environmental Board | url = http://www.keskkonnaamet.ee/public/Keskkonnaharidus/trykised/Saaremaa_eng.pdf | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20131029195241/http://www.keskkonnaamet.ee/public/Keskkonnaharidus/trykised/Saaremaa_eng.pdf | archive-date = 2013-10-29 }}</ref>

He served as the president of the [[Estonian Naturalists' Society]] between 1973 and 1976 and was an honorary member of the society from 1988.<ref name="MOE"/>  Between 1973 and 1981 he was also the academic secretary in the Department of Chemical, Geological and Biological Sciences of the [[Estonian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="MOE"/> He would later work as a Professor of Botany and Ecology at the [[University of Tartu]] from 1987 to 1995.

Parmasto worked as the senior researcher in the Mycology Department of the Institute of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences at the [[Estonian University of Life Sciences]].<ref name="MOE"/>

==Awards==
He was a recipient of the [[Karl Ernst von Baer medal]] in 1976. In 1994 he won the National Science Prize from the Yearly Award, Culture and Society, and in 2002, was awarded the honorable Lifetime Achievement Award in Biosciences and the Environment again. In 2008 he was given the [[Eerik Kumari Award]] for his contributions to Bioscience. Jaanus Kala, Deputy Secretary-General of the Ministry of the Environment and chairman of the award's jury said of the scientist, “Erast Parmasto has dedicated his life’s work to studying nature and to promoting its protection among the public”.<ref name="MOE"/>

In 1964, Czech mycologists [[František Kotlaba]] and [[Zdenek Pouzar]], together [[circumscription (taxonomy)|circumscribed]] the fungal genus of ''[[Parmastomyces]]'' (in the family [[Fomitopsidaceae]]), it was named in his honour.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Kotlába, F. |author2=Pouzar, Z. |year=1964 |title=Staining spores of Homobasidiomycetes in cotton blue and its importance for taxonomy |journal=Feddes Repertorium Specierum Novarum Regni Vegetabilis |volume=69 |pages=131–142}}</ref>

''[[Erastia]]'' is a fungal [[genus]] in the family [[Polyporaceae]]. It is a [[monotypic]] genus, containing the single European species '''''Erastia salmonicolor'''''. ''Erastia'' was [[circumscription (taxonomy)|circumscribed]] by Finnish mycologists Tuomo Niemelä and Juha Kinnunen in 2005 and also named in his honour.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Niemelä, T. |author2=Kinnunen, J. |author3=Larsson, K.H. |author4=Schigel, D.D. |author5=Larsson, E. |year=2005 |title=Genus revisions and new combinations of some North European polypores |journal=Karstenia |volume=45 |issue=2 |pages=75–80 |doi=10.29203/ka.2005.406 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/262184762|doi-access=free }}</ref>
